{{Quote|Telerath is what the galaxy forgot it wanted in a bank!|Planetary slogan|<ref name="KOTOR11">[[Knights of the Old Republic 11|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 11]]</ref>}}
'''Telerath''' was an [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] banking [[Planet/Legends|world]], the home of the [[Telerath Interstellar Banking Initiative]]. It was created as an experiment in face-to-face customer service by an interstellar [[Bank/Legends|bank]]. Customers were guaranteed to meet with living bank representatives, did not need to make scheduled appointments, and were offered a fantastic variety of comforting recreational activities and accommodations.

==Description==
{{Quote|They say few places are finer than Telerath. Feel that warm, tropical air. Look at that glorious sunlight.|[[Beyghor Sahdett]]|<ref name="OutOfWilderness1">[[Dark Times—Out of the Wilderness 1|''Dark Times—Out of the Wilderness'' 1]]</ref>}}
Telerath was a bank and a vacation resort where every night was like a festival. Security was only present to protect the money, not the people. They thought that visible guards would break the ambiance.

==History==
{{Quote|Telerath is an experiment by an interstellar bank in ''face-to-face'' customer service. We offer all the financial services of an Aargau&mdash;without the cold and impersonal touch you find at many banks closer to the core.|[[GG-36]]|<ref name="KOTOR11" />}}
[[File:Telerath_long.jpg|left|thumb|218x218px|Telerath]]
In [[3963 BBY]], it was visited by [[Zayne Carrick]] and the crew of [[The Last Resort (starship)|''The Last Resort'']] in an attempt to access one of [[Marn Hierogryph]]'s many accounts. Due to the [[Padawan Massacre]] of [[Taris/Legends|Taris]], one of them was frozen and because Gryph was a wanted criminal, he had two [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanian]] [[Arkanian Offshoot/Legends|Offshoots]] [[Jarael]] and [[Gorman Vandrayk|Camper]], as "Chantique" and "Baron Hyro Margryph" respectively to unfreeze the account to say it was a name misconception. The ploy was successful and the account was unfrozen. However, the [[Moomo Brothers]] kidnapped their banker, [[Arvan Carrick]], misinterpreting their [[Raana Tey|employer's]] order to simply watch him. The Arkanians were able to avoid a panic by saying Arvan's [[Reiva Carrick|wife]] is having a baby. Because the banker was going to be missed the next day, the Moomos' employer ordered them to head to orbit. Luckily, Arvan was saved by Zayne before that could happen. When the [[Courageous (Inexpugnable-class)|''Courageous'']] was [[Battle of Serroco|destroyed]] over [[Serroco]], Telerath was in a panic.

After the [[Mandalorian Wars]], Telerath became forgotten. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and after, Telerath was rediscovered, and some attempted to turn the planet into a vacation destination. As Telerath was populated again, an archipelago-town called [[Noua]] was founded. Despite Telerath's inhabitants being known primarily as bankers and vacationers, much of the indigenous population lived in fear of, or became part of, two rival gangs that ruled the planet. These two groups were known locally as simply the [[Ken-Kiba's spice runner gang|Spicers]] and the [[Musori's gang|enlavers]], both named after that which they trafficked in most. Though the gangs strictly followed and enforced the [[Sword law]], a law stating that all disputes had to be settled with [[Sword/Legends|swords]], not [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]], a simmering hatred of one another was always ready to boil over. After the arrival of fugitive [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], [[Dass Jennir]], open [[Skirmish on Telerath|warfare]] erupted between the two gangs, with the [[T'surr (species)|T'surr]]-run Spicers coming out ahead. As chaos and violence wracked the city of Noua, Jennir attacked the assembled Spicer gang alone, intent on stopping their criminal rule. Jennir annihilated the Spicers and departed the planet a short time later. After that the inhabitants of Telerath founded a [[Militia]] to make sure that they wouldn't be subjugated by criminals again,

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Telerath&mdash;your bank's customer service center by way of Disneyland&mdash;was a different take on the notion of the banking planet, and Brian Ching brought it to amazing life.|John Jackson Miller|<ref name="Faraway KotOR 11">{{Faraway|url=comics/swknights/swkotor11.html|text=''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic #11''}}</ref>}}
Telerath first appeared in the [[Knights of the Old Republic 11|eleventh issue]] of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (comic series)|''Knights of the Old Republic'']], written by [[John Jackson Miller]], penciled by [[Brian Ching]], and published by [[Dark Horse Comics]]<ref name="KotOR 11">[[Knights of the Old Republic 11|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 11]]</ref> on [[December 27]], [[2006]].<ref name="Marvel KOTOR11">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54330/star_wars_knights_of_the_old_republic_2006_11|text=Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (2006) #11}}</ref> The planet, described by Miller as a bank's customer service center by way of [[Wikipedia:Disneyland|Disneyland]], was intended to be a different approach to a banking world to that of [[Aargau/Legends|Aargau]] from the [[Marvel Comics|Marvel]] [[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'']] comic series. Miller described the bank as having a mountainous central tower and stretching across countryside, while Ching added a sea and several other islands to the landscape. Miller stated that after working with the name Telerath for some time, he realized its pronunciation unintentionally resembled "teller wrath," noting that it may be the reason the bank had chosen it.<ref name="Faraway KotOR 11" />
